transcript: Two things that nobody told me before seeing this play. One is that it's kind of a mystery who done it. And two is that it might spark some reflective conversation if you see it with your friends. As the title suggests, all nighter is a new play about a group of college seniors who gather in the library to pull one last all nighter before finals. As you might expect, tensions arise, friendships are challenged, and like I said, there's a little bit of a mystery element that runs through the play as well. The reason I'm highlighting that one component of the play is partly because I just like that sort of thing and it was a fun surprise, but also because I think it helps set the play apart from others of its kind. We see a lot of these plays where it like, all takes place in one room and the drama ensues when old secrets come to light. And it sometimes it can feel like the plot has been front loaded. Like all of the actual drama happened before the play even started, and now we're just hearing about it and watching them find out about it, which I know is like the classic formula for a play going all the way back to the ancient Greeks. But sometimes I just don't think it's that interesting. And there is a lot of that in this play, but there is also a sense of immediacy that Comes from some events that actually do unfold during the course of the play. The other thing I mentioned that caught me off guard was the experience of seeing this show with one of my best friends, because the play offers some thought provoking insight on the nature of close friendships, where sometimes within a friend group, people are very quick to employ a kind of radical empathy to rationalize everything the others do or say. There's a line in this play where she says, there's always something to understand, and especially with your friends, because they're in your corner, they're your support system. And this play sort of asked the question of where is that line? I had this interesting conversation with my friend afterward about, like, what would we do if something like this in the play happened within our friend group? So I think a lot of people might connect to this play like I did, and I also just found it pretty entertaining. So if you think this might be up your alley, it's currently running through May 18th.
